key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 perovskites strongly tunes stability, bandgap, and solar-cell performance, with the iodide variant emerging as the best photovoltaic candidate.
engineering_relevance: This study highlights composition engineering as a practical route to optimize perovskite-like materials for more efficient optoelectronic and solar energy devices.
method: Band structure and optical analysis across X = F, Cl, Br, I
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps from 2.0 to 3.788 eV and SLME results up to 29.6% for Ca3PI3, while Ca3PF3 is much lower at 0.6%.
watch_item: The high predicted efficiency is computational and should be validated experimentally, especially for synthesis stability and real-device losses.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
